name: Main Point and the Strip
tagline: The single sandy street beside the point break
description: Arugam Bay is essentially one road running parallel to the beach, and this is the busy end of it, next to the point break that made the place. Guesthouses, surf shops, bars and restaurants line both sides, and everything happens within a few hundred metres.
bestFor: Anyone here to surf, with the break and the bars both a minute away
pros: All bars, restaurants and surf shops on one street
The whole social scene of the town
cons: Loud until late through the season
The highest rents in the bay, in season

name: South End and Ullae
tagline: The quieter end of the strip, towards the lagoon
description: The southern stretch of the road towards the lagoon and the bridge, with guesthouses set further back among the palms, a wider and emptier beach, and considerably less noise. It is a ten-minute walk to the point and a different atmosphere entirely.
bestFor: Stays that want the beach and the surf without the strip's volume
pros: Much quieter while still walkable to the point
Lower rents than the main strip
cons: Ten minutes to the surf shops and bars
Mosquitoes from the lagoon at dusk

name: Pottuvil
tagline: The working town three kilometres north
description: The actual town the bay belongs to, north across the lagoon bridge, with the market, the banks, the bus station and a Muslim and Tamil population going about ordinary business. It is where you shop properly, and rents are a fraction of the beach strip.
bestFor: Long stays wanting local prices and a town that stays open all year
pros: Market, banks and buses, at local prices
The lowest rents in the area
cons: Conservative, so dress and behaviour matter

name: Whiskey Point and Peanut Farm
tagline: The outlying breaks, reached by tuk-tuk
description: The secondary surf spots north and south of the bay, each with a handful of cabanas and a beach shack or two and nothing else. They work at different swell sizes from the main point, which is why people move between them, and they are considerably emptier.
bestFor: Surfers who want an emptier line-up and do not mind the ride
pros: Far fewer people in the water
Beach shacks and simple cabanas right at the break
cons: A tuk-tuk or scooter is essential
Almost no services and weak connectivity

name: Panama Village (12 km south)
tagline: The last village, at the edge of Kumana park
description: A small fishing and farming village twelve kilometres south, the last settlement before Kumana National Park, with elephants crossing the road at dusk and the empty beaches of Elephant Rock and Okanda nearby. Nothing here but a few homestays and the park entrance.
bestFor: Stays that want the park and the wildlife more than the surf scene
pros: Kumana National Park and its wildlife at the door
Empty beaches at Elephant Rock and Okanda
Very low costs and genuine village life
cons: Elephants on the road at dusk are a real hazard
Twenty to thirty minutes to Arugam Bay
